kept.claim: `website_name` bypasses the TL0/anonymous `untrusted_attributes` restriction that hides `website`, so restricted users' website host/path is still serialized and rendered. The attempted guard `include_website_name` also lacks the `?` AMS 0.8 requires, so it is never called.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] `website_name` leaks the website that `untrusted_attributes` hides for TL0 users

**Severity:** HIGH -- the anti-spam/privacy restriction on TL0 profile websites no longer works; anonymous visitors see the (linked) website again.

### The Problem
```ruby
untrusted_attributes :bio_raw, :bio_cooked, :bio_excerpt, :location,
                     :website, :profile_background, :card_background
...
def include_website_name
  website.present?
end
```
`website` is an untrusted attribute (lines 104-110). Its generated guard (lines 24-30) returns `false` when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`, i.e. `user.trust_level == TrustLevel[0] && anonymous?` (`lib/guardian/user_guardian.rb:58-60`). The new `website_name` is not in that list, and its own guard can't run because it is named without the `?`.

### Theory / Proof
- ActiveModel::Serializers 0.8.3 (`Gemfile.lock:22`) only calls `include_<attr>?`. Every working guard in this file uses that form (the metaprogrammed ones at lines 9/18/27, `include_email?` at line 117, and others). `include_website_name` is a plain method nobody calls, so `website_name` is always emitted.
- Even with the `?`, `website.present?` calls the serializer's `website` method, which reads `object.user_profile.website` directly and ignores the untrusted guard. So renaming alone would not fix the leak.
- `user.hbs` now tests `{{#if model.website_name}}` rather than `model.website`, so for an anonymous visitor on a TL0 profile it renders the globe icon and the host/path text, and the `<a href={{model.website}}>` link with an empty href.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Before this PR, `website` was dropped for TL0 users viewed anonymously, and the client-side `websiteName` (derived from `model.website`) was empty, so nothing showed. After this PR, a spammer's freshly created TL0 account shows `spam-site.com/landing` to every logged-out visitor, which is the case the restriction exists to prevent. None of the new specs cover a TL0 user viewed anonymously.

### Research
AMS 0.8 README, "Conditional attributes": define `include_<attribute>?`. The existing `untrusted_attributes` helper in this same file is the pattern to follow.

### Recommendation
Put `website_name` under the same restriction and drop the broken hand-written guard:
```ruby
untrusted_attributes :bio_raw,
                     :bio_cooked,
                     :bio_excerpt,
                     :location,
                     :website,
                     :website_name,
                     :profile_background,
                     :card_background
```
(the generated `include_website_name?` returns `false` for restricted users and otherwise `website_name.present?`), and remove `def include_website_name`. Add a spec: a TL0 user serialized with `Guardian.new` (anonymous) must not have `:website_name`.
kept.evidence: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 defines `include_website_name` with no `?`. Every other guard in the file uses the `include_<attr>?` form (lines 9, 18, 27, 117 and others), which is the AMS 0.8 convention, and Gemfile.lock:22 pins 0.8.3, so this method is never called. The validator also found that `website` is in `untrusted_attributes` (lines 104-110; guard at lines 24-30 returns false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`, which is TL0 viewed by anonymous per lib/guardian/user_guardian.rb:58-60) but `website_name` is not. So the new field sends the host/path that the restriction is meant to hide, and user.hbs now renders it. I confirmed this in the code.

kept.claim: If the stored website is not parseable by `URI()` (e.g. contains a space or non-ASCII IDN characters), `website_name` becomes nil and the template now hides the website entirely, a regression from the old client-side `split('/')[2]` which always displayed something.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Unparseable website URLs now disappear from the profile

**Severity:** MEDIUM -- users with a saved website that `URI()` rejects lose the website line on their profile entirely.

### The Problem
```ruby
website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil
...
return if website_host.nil?
```
and in `user.hbs`:
```hbs
{{#if model.website_name}}
```
Any `URI::InvalidURIError` is swallowed and `website_name` is nil, so the whole globe icon + link block is skipped.

### Theory / Proof
- The website is stored with no validation: `UserUpdater#format_url` (`app/services/user_updater.rb:105-106`) only prefixes `http://` and `UserProfile` has no format validation on `website`.
- Ruby's `URI()` uses the RFC 3986 parser, which raises `URI::InvalidURIError` for unescaped spaces (`http://example.com/my page`), non-ASCII hostnames (`http://muller-with-umlaut.de`), `|`, `{`, etc.
- The removed client code `website.split("/")[2]` produced a host for all of these inputs.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Before this PR, a user who typed `example.com/my page` saw `example.com` on their profile. After this PR, nothing is shown at all -- the website field silently vanishes, even though it is still saved and visible in preferences.

### Research
Ruby docs for `URI::RFC3986_Parser#parse` -- raises `InvalidURIError` on characters outside RFC 3986. `Addressable::URI` (already a Discourse dependency via other gems) accepts IDNs and is more lenient.

### Recommendation
Fall back to the raw host extraction instead of dropping the value:
```ruby
def website_name
  uri = URI(website.to_s) rescue nil
  website_host = uri.try(:host) || website.to_s.split("/")[2]
  return if website_host.blank?
  ...
end
```
(and only append `uri.path` when `uri` is present).
kept.evidence: user_serializer.rb:138-140: `rescue nil` swallows URI::InvalidURIError (unescaped spaces, non-ASCII), then line 140 returns nil. user_updater.rb:31,105-107 only prefixes http://, and user_profile.rb has no website validation. user.hbs `{{#if model.website_name}}` hides the block, whereas the removed `website.split('/')[2]` showed a host.

kept.claim: Host comparisons are case-sensitive; `URI#host` preserves case, so a website like `http://Example.com/user` on instance `example.com` does not get the full path.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Hostname comparison is case-sensitive

**Severity:** LOW -- inconsistent display for mixed-case URLs.

### The Problem
```ruby
if website_host == discourse_host
...
discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)
```
`URI("http://Example.com/user").host` returns `"Example.com"` (case preserved), and `format_url` in `app/services/user_updater.rb:106` does not normalize case.

### Theory / Proof
RFC 3986 section 3.2.2 and RFC 4343: the host component is case-insensitive. Comparing with `==` treats `Example.com` and `example.com` as different domains.

### What happens today vs. what will break
A user who types `Example.com/about` (common with mobile auto-capitalization) on the `example.com` forum sees only `Example.com` instead of `Example.com/about`, contradicting the feature's intent.

### Research
Rails' own host checks (`ActionDispatch::HostAuthorization`) downcase before comparing.

### Recommendation
```ruby
website_host = (URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil).try(:downcase)
discourse_host = Discourse.current_hostname.downcase
```
kept.evidence: user_serializer.rb:141,146,149 compare hosts case-sensitively. URI::Generic keeps host case unless `normalize` is called, which it isn't. format_url (user_updater.rb:105-107) doesn't downcase. `Discourse.current_hostname` (lib/discourse.rb:178-184) returns the setting unchanged.

kept.claim: The sibling-subdomain heuristic strips only the first label, so unrelated sites under a shared multi-label public suffix (e.g. `alice.co.uk` vs instance `forum.co.uk`, or `a.herokuapp.com` vs `b.herokuapp.com`) are treated as the same site.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] "Same parent domain" heuristic ignores public suffixes

**Severity:** LOW -- display-only, but the heuristic misclassifies unrelated domains.

### The Problem
```ruby
elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2
  website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host
```
For instance `forum.co.uk` and website `http://alice.co.uk/x`, both have 3 labels and both strip to `co.uk`, so the full path is shown as if `alice.co.uk` were the forum's own site. Same for `*.herokuapp.com`, `*.github.io`, `*.com.au`.

Conversely, `blog.example.com` vs instance `example.com` hits the `else` branch and `example.com.ends_with?(".blog.example.com")` is false, so a subdomain of the instance only shows the host -- the relationship is only detected in one direction.

### Theory / Proof
Registrable domains are defined by the Public Suffix List (publicsuffix.org), not by label count. Label counting is a known-wrong approximation.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Common `example.com`/`www.example.com`/`forum.example.com` setups work. Instances on ccTLD second-level domains or shared hosting suffixes get paths for unrelated users' sites.

### Research
The `public_suffix` gem (`PublicSuffix.domain(host)`) is the standard Ruby implementation of the Public Suffix List. Note that it is not currently in `Gemfile.lock`, so using it adds a dependency.

### Recommendation
Either compare registrable domains (adds the `public_suffix` gem):
```ruby
same_site = (PublicSuffix.domain(website_host) == PublicSuffix.domain(discourse_host)) rescue false
same_site ? website_host + uri.path : website_host
```
which also collapses the three branches into one, or, with no new dependency, limit the full-path case to exact match or one host being a dot-suffix of the other in either direction:
```ruby
related = website_host == discourse_host ||
          discourse_host.end_with?(".#{website_host}") ||
          website_host.end_with?(".#{discourse_host}")
```
kept.evidence: user_serializer.rb:144-146 drops only the first label: alice.co.uk vs forum.co.uk and a.herokuapp.com vs b.herokuapp.com both match. blog.example.com vs example.com falls through to line 149 and gets host only. Display only, so LOW. Caveat: public_suffix is not in Gemfile/Gemfile.lock, so the suggested fix would add a dependency.
